text:
emma: Quick kickoff — we need a concrete set of performance acceptance criteria for the Snowflake + Databricks connector + Qdrant vector integration before marketplace listing. Scope: retrieval latency, end-to-end generation latency, embedding indexing time, and resource/cost envelopes. Launch target: 2026-04-15. Who can own drafting the doc?

raj: I can own the technical acceptance criteria. Proposing initial SLOs: p50 end-to-end (retrieve + generate) <= 180ms for short queries (<= 64 tokens), p95 <= 450ms; indexing throughput >= 50k docs/hour on r5-like instance; max cold-start recovery <= 30s. These are starting points.

tomas: I'll own the benchmark harness and infra runs. We'll need a reproducible matrix: dataset size (10k / 100k / 1M), vector dimensionality (1536), retrieval fanout (k=5,10), model variants (fp16 / int8), and connector modes (direct Snowflake vector UDF vs Databricks external table + qdrant).

zoe: Add quality regression guardrails: recall@10 >= 0.85 on our retrieval evals, and generation divergence delta <= 2% measured by ROUGE-L on the canonical prompt set when switching quantization. If int8 causes >2% drop, it's a fail for default config (can be opt-in).

claire: Marketing needs customer-facing numbers: "avg latency (p50/p95) for retrieval+generation on standard query", "index build time for 100k docs", and a simple cost estimate per 1k requests. Also we need a short blurb about data flow for the marketplace listing.

mike: Solution-eng notes — demo requirements: live indexing of a 50k doc corpus in <20 minutes on a single c6i.xlarge-ish node would be a strong demo. Also include a failure-mode section: if Qdrant node OOMs, fallback path should return cached embeddings or degrade to smaller chunking.

emma: Action items: raj = technical criteria doc (due 3/28), tomas = benchmark harness + sample configs (due 3/30), zoe = quality thresholds + eval scripts (due 3/30), claire = marketing copy + marketplace data flow diagram (due 4/2), mike = demo checklist (due 4/2).

raj: For reproducible runs, use this command pattern (infra-bot will spawn infra):
```
./run_benchmark --dataset wiki-100k --vectors 1536 --model redwood-1-small --quant int8 --retrieval_k 10 --runners 8
```
We'll version the config in partner-integration/benchmarks.

infra-bot: Scheduled benchmark job #452 to run on 2026-03-29 22:00 UTC (queue: partner-integ). Logs will be at s3://redwood-partner-bench/452/.

tomas: Note about connectors — Snowflake external function path adds ~30-60ms on average due to network hop; Databricks UDF path is typically faster in our internal tests but has higher burst cost. We'll quantify both.

zoe: Also watch memory for KV cache during long-context runs. If customers use 2048-context, throughput drops significantly; add a complexity note and recommended limits.

claire: Legal/partner comms: we should coordinate announcement with Snowflake/Databricks partner PMs. I can draft an outreach template. @emma can you confirm contacts and timeline?

emma: I'll loop in partner contacts after raj's doc is up. We should aim to share performance summary with partners by 2026-04-05.

mike: Quick Q: do we want to include Pinecone as a fallback vector DB in the matrix or focus only on Qdrant for initial launch?

raj: Let's keep Pinecone in an "alternate" column but initial certification only for Qdrant. If we get early wins, we can broaden.

claire: +1. Also we should lock messaging around "certified for marketplace" vs "tested" — marketing wants only certified variants in the listing.

emma: Good call. Last note — testing checklist should include: reproducible seed, exact model artifact hash, connector version, and network topology. Put everything in partner-integration/acceptance/criteria.md.

tomas: I'll add a small sample results matrix to the repo after the first run.

emma: thanks team — I'll create the repo skeleton and add tasks. :raised_hands:
